about: Scam patterns published by official US sources, expressed as machine-checkable conditions. Each pattern carries the official guidance it is based on: page URL, a short verbatim quote, and the date the page was read. The rule engine evaluates these conditions deterministically; no language model is involved in a verdict.

condition_language.method_in: payment_method is one of the listed values
condition_language.channel_in: contact_channel is one of the listed values
condition_language.claim_in: urgency_claims contains one of the listed values
condition_language.flag: the named boolean input is true
condition_language.payee_category_in: the named payee resolves to a registry entry in one of these categories, or the request text uses words from the matching lexicon
condition_language.text: the description, summary or payee name contains a whole-word phrase from the named lexicon

gift_card: numbers on the back of the card

patterns.label: Asked to pay with gift cards or a prepaid card
patterns.why: Gift cards are for gifts. Real businesses and government agencies do not ask to be paid with them.

guidance.title: Avoiding and Reporting Gift Card Scams
guidance.quote: No real business or government agency will ever tell you to buy a gift card to pay them.

guidance.title: Taxpayers shouldn’t let gift card scammers ruin the holidays
guidance.quote: the IRS never asks for or accepts gift cards as payment for a tax bill

guidance.title: What are some classic warning signs of possible fraud and scams?
guidance.quote: Tells you to send money using methods like wire transfers, cryptocurrency, payment apps, prepaid cards, or gift cards.

patterns.label: Someone claiming to be from the government is demanding money
patterns.why: Government agencies do not call, text or email to demand money, and they do not threaten arrest over the phone.

guidance.title: How To Avoid a Government Impersonation Scam
guidance.quote: Government agencies will never call, email, text, or message you on social media to ask for money or personal information.

guidance.title: What should I do if I receive a call from someone claiming to be a Social Security employee?
guidance.quote: Threaten you with arrest of legal action.

guidance.title: How to know it’s the IRS
guidance.quote: We normally contact you the first time by mail delivered by the U.S. Postal Service.

guidance.title: 2025 IC3 Annual Report, Appendix B: Definitions
guidance.quote: Government Impersonation: A government official is impersonated to collect or extort money.

patterns.label: Told to keep the payment secret
patterns.why: Being told not to tell family or friends is a strong warning sign. Honest requests can be talked over with someone you trust.

guidance.title: Scammers Use Fake Emergencies To Steal Your Money
guidance.quote: The scammer might tell you it’s important to keep it secret.

guidance.title: Protect Yourself from Scams
guidance.quote: Demand secrecy.

patterns.label: Asked to pay with cryptocurrency or at a crypto ATM
patterns.why: Being told to pay someone in cryptocurrency, or to put cash into a crypto ATM, is a known scam pattern.

guidance.title: What To Know About Cryptocurrency and Scams
guidance.quote: Only scammers demand payment in cryptocurrency.

guidance.title: What To Know About Cryptocurrency and Scams
guidance.quote: Some scammers even stay on the phone with you as they direct you to a cryptocurrency ATM

guidance.title: 2025 IC3 Annual Report: Cryptocurrency ATMs/Kiosks
guidance.quote: 13,460 Complaints; $389 million in Losses

patterns.label: Urgent money for a family member in trouble
patterns.why: Scammers imitate relatives who need bail or emergency money. Checking with another family member first is the recommended step.

guidance.title: Scammers Use Fake Emergencies To Steal Your Money
guidance.quote: Resist the pressure to react and send money immediately.

guidance.title: Scammers Use Fake Emergencies To Steal Your Money
guidance.quote: Call someone else in your family or circle of friends, even if the caller said to keep it a secret

guidance.title: 2025 IC3 Annual Report
guidance.quote: grandparent scams, or “distress” scams, in which voice cloning technology is used to mimic the sound of a loved one in distress

guidance.title: What are some classic warning signs of possible fraud and scams?
guidance.quote: Beware when someone plays on your emotions or claims there’s an urgent situation.

patterns.label: Unexpected tech support asking for payment or remote access
patterns.why: Real tech companies do not contact people out of the blue about a computer problem, and real warnings do not ask you to call a number.

guidance.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams
guidance.quote: Legitimate tech companies won’t contact you by phone, email, or text message to tell you there’s a problem with your computer.

guidance.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams
guidance.quote: Real security pop-up warnings and messages will never ask you to call a phone number.

guidance.title: 2025 IC3 Annual Report, Appendix B: Definitions
guidance.quote: Tech/Customer Support Fraud: Subject posing as technical or customer support/service.

patterns.label: Asked to send back an overpayment or an accidental refund
patterns.why: Being sent too much money and asked to return the difference is a known scam. The original payment usually turns out to be fake.

guidance.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Fake Check Scams
guidance.quote: Never use money from a check to send gift cards, money orders, cryptocurrency, or to wire money to anyone who asks you to.

guidance.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams
guidance.quote: They say they refunded you too much money and insist you pay them back

guidance.title: 2025 IC3 Annual Report, Appendix B: Definitions
guidance.quote: An individual is sent a payment/commission and is instructed to keep a portion of the payment and send the remainder to another individual or business.

patterns.label: Asked to pay a fee or taxes to collect a prize
patterns.why: Real prizes are free. Being asked to pay fees or taxes first to collect winnings is a known scam pattern.

guidance.title: Fake Prize, Sweepstakes, and Lottery Scams
guidance.quote: If you have to pay to get your prize, it’s a scam. Real prizes are free.

guidance.title: What are some classic warning signs of possible fraud and scams?
guidance.quote: Never pay up front for a prize or offer. It’s a scam if you are told that you must pay fees or taxes first.

guidance.title: 2025 IC3 Annual Report, Appendix B: Definitions
guidance.quote: An individual is contacted about winning a lottery or sweepstakes they never entered

patterns.label: Asked to pay for a Medicare card
patterns.why: Medicare cards are sent automatically and free of charge. Medicare does not call to sell anything or charge for a card.

guidance.title: How To Avoid a Government Impersonation Scam
guidance.quote: Medicare won’t call, email, text, or message you on social media to sell you anything or tell you to pay for your Medicare card.

guidance.title: Your Medicare card
guidance.quote: Medicare will never call you uninvited and ask you to give us personal or private information.

patterns.label: Threat to shut off a utility unless paid right away
patterns.why: Real utility companies do not call, text or visit to demand immediate payment to avoid a same-day shutoff.

guidance.title: Scammers Pretend To Be Your Utility Company
guidance.quote: real utility companies won’t demand immediate payment to avoid same-day disconnection

guidance.title: Scammers Pretend To Be Your Utility Company
guidance.quote: contact your utility company using the number on your bill or the company’s website

guidance.title: 10th annual Utility Scam Awareness Day
guidance.quote: Scammers may demand immediate payment or threaten service cut-off, but we will never do that.

patterns.label: Told to move money or hand over cash or gold to keep it safe
patterns.why: No government agency or bank asks people to move savings to a safe account, or to hand cash or gold to a courier.

guidance.title: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams
guidance.quote: Someone who works for the government will never tell you to put your money in a federal safety locker.

guidance.title: Protect Yourself from Scams
guidance.quote: Tell you to move your money to a protected bank account to keep it safe.

guidance.title: Protect Yourself from Scams
guidance.quote: Meet you in-person to pick up cash, gold bars, or other assets.

patterns.label: Pressure to pay right away
patterns.why: Being rushed is a common warning sign. Honest businesses give people time to think and to ask someone they trust.

guidance.title: How To Avoid a Scam
guidance.quote: Scammers want you to act before you have time to think.

guidance.title: How To Avoid a Scam
guidance.quote: Honest businesses will give you time to make a decision.

guidance.title: What are some classic warning signs of possible fraud and scams?
guidance.quote: Pressures you to act right away by telling you the deal won’t last, or doesn’t give you time to ask questions.

guidance.title: Protect Yourself from Scams
guidance.quote: Take a deep breath and talk to someone you trust.
